# War Scroll Column 13 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 13 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 13:1 — "without one to bury" vs. "without burial" vs. "with no one to bury them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "without-one-to-bury" | Literal participial construction |
| LOGOS | "without burial" | Concise formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "with no one to bury them" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "without burial" (LOGOS). Concise and clear; EMET's hyphenation is awkward; PNEUMA's expansion is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:1-2 — "mighty man of valor" vs. "mighty warrior" vs. "great champion"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-mighty-man of-valor" | Literal rendering of gibbor chayil |
| LOGOS | "a mighty warrior" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "that great champion" | Dynamic rendering with demonstrative |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a mighty warrior" (LOGOS). EMET's full construct is verbose; PNEUMA's "great champion" loses the Hebrew military term gibbor.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:3 — "Your great holiness" vs. "Your supreme holiness" — divine attribute

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Your-great-holiness" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "Your great holiness" | Same, unhyphenated |
| PNEUMA | "Your supreme holiness" | Elevated register |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Your great holiness" (EMET/LOGOS). "Supreme" is interpretive elevation not warranted by the Hebrew gadol.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:4-5 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love" — hesed rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "covenant-faithfulness" | Project convention |
| LOGOS | "covenant-faithfulness" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "faithful love" | Dynamic rendering of hesed |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "covenant-faithfulness" (EMET/LOGOS). Project convention; consistency required.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:6 — "the might" vs. "the power" — duplication avoidance

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-might" | Literal rendering of gevurah |
| LOGOS | "the power" | Avoids repeating "might" from "strength" |
| PNEUMA | "the power" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the power" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). Avoids immediate repetition with "strength" in the same clause.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 13:7 — "told us" vs. "declared to us" vs. "told us this promise"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "told-us" | Simple literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "declared to us" | Formal prophetic register |
| PNEUMA | "told us this promise" | Added "this promise" for context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "declared to us" (LOGOS). Appropriate register for introducing a scriptural citation; PNEUMA adds without textual warrant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:8 — "step forth" vs. "march forth" vs. "come out" — Star Prophecy verb

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall-step-forth" | Literal rendering of darakh, "to tread/step" |
| LOGOS | "shall march forth" | Martial connotation appropriate to context |
| PNEUMA | "will come out" | Simplified rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "shall march forth" (LOGOS). darakh carries a martial sense ("to tread, march"); "march forth" captures this in context. PNEUMA's "come out" is too weak for the messianic prophecy.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:8 — "temples" vs. "brow" vs. "skull" — anatomical term in Numbers 24:17

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-temples" | Literal rendering of pa'atey (sides of head) |
| LOGOS | "the brow" | Standard formal rendering of pa'atey Moab |
| PNEUMA | "the skull" | Vivid dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the brow" (LOGOS). pa'atey refers to the sides/corners of the head; "brow" is a recognized English rendering. "Skull" (PNEUMA) is too violent an expansion; "temples" (EMET) is anatomically precise but unfamiliar in biblical English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:10 — "prince of the dominion of wickedness" vs. "chief of the kingdom of evil"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-prince of-the-dominion of-wickedness" | Literal triple construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the prince of the dominion of wickedness" | Same, standard DSS rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the chief of the kingdom of evil" | Simplified for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the prince of the dominion of wickedness" (EMET/LOGOS). This is the established scholarly designation for Belial in 1QM; altering it loses recognition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:11 — "eternal aid" vs. "eternal help" vs. "help that lasts forever"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "eternal-aid" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "eternal help" | Formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "help that lasts forever" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "eternal aid" (EMET). "Aid" is slightly more formal and martial than "help"; PNEUMA's expansion is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 13:11-12 — "majestic angel" vs. "glorious angel" — angelic epithet

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-majestic angel" | Rendering of mal'akh ha-addir |
| LOGOS | "the majestic angel" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "His glorious angel" | Added possessive; "glorious" for addir |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the majestic angel" (EMET/LOGOS). addir means "majestic/mighty," not primarily "glorious" (kavod). PNEUMA's added possessive is not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:12 — "to illuminate with joy" vs. "to shine in eternal light" vs. "will shine in eternal light"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to-illuminate with-joy the-covenant of-Israel" | Literal infinitive construction |
| LOGOS | "shall shine in eternal light, to illumine with joy the covenant of Israel" | Expanded with two clauses |
| PNEUMA | "will shine in eternal light, bringing joy to Israel's covenant" | Dynamic rephrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing with slight simplification. The text contains both "eternal light" and "joy" elements.

**Status:** Resolved with compromise.

---

## 13:14 — "among all flesh" vs. "above every nation on earth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "among-all flesh" | Literal rendering of be-khol basar |
| LOGOS | "among all flesh" | Same, standard biblical idiom |
| PNEUMA | "above every nation on earth" | Interpretive expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "among all flesh" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a standard biblical idiom; PNEUMA's "above every nation on earth" changes "among" to "above" and "flesh" to "nation."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:15 — "crucible" vs. "refining fire" — testing metaphor

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-crucible of-God" | Literal rendering of kur |
| LOGOS | "God's crucible" | Possessive variant |
| PNEUMA | "God's refining fire" | Interprets the metallurgical metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the crucible of God" (EMET). kur literally means "furnace/crucible"; "refining fire" is an interpretation. The concrete image should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 13:15-16 — "waves His hand" vs. "raises His hand" — divine gesture

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "waves His-hand" | Literal rendering of heniph yado |
| LOGOS | "waves His hand" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "raises His hand" | Simplified gesture |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "waves His hand" (EMET/LOGOS). heniph specifically means "wave/swing," not simply "raise."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:16-17 — "appointed time of His visitation" vs. "the day when He comes"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-appointed-time of-His-visitation" | Literal rendering of mo'ed pequddato |
| LOGOS | "the appointed time of His visitation" | Standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the day when He comes" | Simplified eschatological language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the appointed time of His visitation" (EMET/LOGOS). "Visitation" (pequddah) is a technical theological term in DSS that carries both judgment and salvation; "the day when He comes" loses this nuance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements:** 16
